card.name: Words just before a hyphen or noun in chemistry
card.fires_on: Words in chemistry and compatibility text that come right before a hyphenated or noun continuation, such as phase, two, non, multi, single, fluor. These are places where a word like 'solution' could plausibly follow but the model should not predict it.

modes.label: Phase and separation terms
modes.description: A word like phase or two before separation or separate solids in physical chemistry.
modes.example: (2.5-4.0 mol dm(-3))<< phase>> separation was attained.

modes.label: Prefix before a hyphen
modes.description: A prefix or partial word that leads into a hyphenated compound, as in non-PVC or single-dose.
modes.example: polyvinylchloride (PVC) or<< non>>-PVC polyolefin bags and administration

modes.label: Partway through chemical names
modes.description: The middle of a long drug or material name, such as perflutren or fluorinated.

card.writes: It suppresses 'solution' and its translations, so the model is less likely to continue with that word.
card.plain: It fires on short chemistry words and name parts where the next word is unlikely to be 'solution'.
